summary: Baseline tests passed, but the implementation missed six explicit integrity and persistence requirements in the new maintenance tests.

details.reasoning: The code runs and passes all 42 baseline tests, but six of 143 new tests fail. The failures correspond directly to specified behavior: rejecting fail initialization briefly creates an absent index; saves cannot update through an entry-recorded symlink; custom strategies receive normalized rather than unchanged descriptions; entries reaching the same outside file through different paths are not shared; a backslash immediately before a carriage return is lost; and a hard link to the index is not rejected as an index alias. The added existing-test changes only add coverage, and no cheating or test weakening was detected.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's optional Spotless check could not download google-java-format, but the full local test task completed successfully and this did not affect grading.

quick_failure_summary: Six explicit store-integrity edge cases fail despite all baseline tests passing.

justification.issue_description: Several required store-integrity edge cases are implemented incorrectly: fail-mode absent-index handling, symlink and hard-link ownership/safety, raw strategy descriptions, outside-file sharing, and preservation of backslash-plus-carriage-return violation text.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says that fail rejection does not even create an absent index, that saves write through a file/link recorded by the rule but never over the index or another file identity, that entries resolving to one file are shared even outside the folder, and that a carriage return inside stored violation text remains part of that text. In the patch, initializeUnderLock creates the index at lines 180-183 before fail inspection; save uses isRegularDirectFile(..., NOFOLLOW_LINKS) and only path equality at lines 337-347; save normalizes the rule description at line 312 before invoking the strategy; directPathFor rejects outside paths at lines 845-855; and unescape removes backslash-carriage-return pairs at lines 796-802.
justification.verdict_reasoning: These are not undocumented test conventions: each behavior is stated in the task, and the verifier executes successfully far enough to report ordinary assertion and exception failures. A competent implementer should preserve these explicitly specified semantics, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is more appropriate than an environment or test-harness verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is complex but solvable and fair. The six failing tests exercise detailed behaviors that are explicitly described, and the reference implementation confirms the requirements are implementable.

evidence: The test execution log reports a successful baseline run of 42/42 and a completed new run of 137/143, with six normal test failures and no bootstrap errors.
JUnit XML reports 0 baseline failures/errors and exactly 6 new-test failures/errors, all with assertions or expected store exceptions.
The trajectory shows the agent's full :archunit:test completed successfully; only the optional Spotless task failed after a 6m16s Maven timeout downloading google-java-format.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful runtime, dependency, verifier, or sandbox blocker explains the graded failures; they are implementation defects.
